Definition: properly, to become pale, i.e. (by implication) to pine after; also to fear
BiblicalUsage: Kacaph is longing that pales the face — to pine after, to yearn for what is absent. Laban says Jacob stole away because he sore longed after his father's house; Job says God will have a desire to the work of His hands; and the psalmist cries that his soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe longing is one of the truest things about us. We pine after home and after God because we were made for both — and the ache itself is a signpost pointing me home to Him.
